key_insight: In tungsten, vacancy loops do not behave as fixed obstacles: their interaction with dislocations can annihilate, weaken, transport, or transform them into stronger sessile defects, so obstacle strength evolves during deformation.
engineering_relevance: These atomistic mechanisms provide the missing physical basis for irradiation-hardening constitutive models used to predict fusion reactor structural material performance beyond calibrated conditions.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of edge dislocations interacting with vacancy loops in tungsten
Systematic variation of loop size, crystallographic orientation, and dislocation-loop intersection geometry
Translation of atomistically measured obstacle strengths into mesoscale constitutive parameters
evidence_signal: The study uses simulation results to compare interaction outcomes across geometries and demonstrates a framework for converting those outcomes into irradiation-hardening inputs for constitutive models.
watch_item: The proposed constitutive parameters are derived from atomistic conditions, so model transferability to real reactor microstructures will require careful calibration and validation.
paper_title: Evolution of the Irradiation Induced Defect Landscape through Dislocation Vacancy Loop Interactions in Tungsten
